analysis.evidence: In יְהִי אוֹר (“let there be light”), God commands that light exist. The following וַיְהִי אוֹר (“and there was light”) reports the fulfillment of that command.
analysis.morphology: Qal jussive, third person masculine singular, agreeing with אוֹר (“light”) and expressing God’s command.

analysis.evidence: In יְהִי אוֹר, “let there be light,” אוֹר is the subject of the masculine singular jussive יְהִי. The following וַיְהִי אוֹר, “and there was light,” confirms what came into being.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, used here with masculine singular agreement. No prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The command יְהִי אוֹר, “let there be light,” is fulfilled in וַיְהִי אוֹר, “and there was light.” The subject אוֹר names what now exists.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־. The verb agrees with its subject אוֹר.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי אוֹר (“and there was light”), אוֹר is the subject of וַיְהִי. It names the light called for in יְהִי אוֹר (“let there be light”).
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.
